Open a mira plot in the browser

Source: R/mira.R
print.mira_plot.Rd

Starts a local server with the network and its view spec and opens MiRA. Typing a plot's name at the console does this; call print() to choose the port or the browser, or to open the plot in RStudio's Viewer pane (viewer = TRUE, or options(ggmira.viewer = TRUE) for every plot). Each print starts a new server (on the next free port when port is taken), and shows where MiRA is served from, the plot's address (http://localhost:8080?autoload=true) and where to report issues. MiRA loads its drawing libraries from the web, so the plot needs an internet connection.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'mira_plot'
print(
  x,
  port = 8080,
  mira_path = NULL,
  browser = getOption("browser"),
  viewer = getOption("ggmira.viewer", FALSE),
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A mira_plot.

port

Integer. Port for the local HTTP server. Default is 8080.

mira_path

Character. Path to the MiRA web-app directory. If NULL (default), uses the copy bundled with the package (system.file("MiRA", package = "ggmira")).

browser

Choose the specific browser to open MiRA in. Defaults to the system default via getOption("browser"). A command that opens a page, as for browseURL: a browser's name where that is a command (e.g. "firefox" on Linux), or on macOS "open -a Firefox". "chrome" works on macOS too. When R is not interactive (a script), a plot opens only when browser is given.

viewer

TRUE to open MiRA in RStudio's Viewer pane instead of the browser (outside RStudio, the browser opens). Defaults to FALSE, or to getOption("ggmira.viewer"): put options(ggmira.viewer = TRUE) in your .Rprofile to always use the pane (the option must be TRUE or FALSE; anything else is an error). A browser given in the call wins. MiRA needs room (at least 1024 x 600 pixels): maximize the pane, or click its Show in new window button to move the plot to the browser.

...

Not used.

Value

Invisibly, the server handle. Stop it with httpuv::stopServer(handle), or stop all servers with httpuv::stopAllServers(). NULL when nothing was opened (R is not interactive and browser was not given).

Details

In a script. When R is not interactive (Rscript, R Markdown, R CMD check) nothing opens and print() returns NULL, with a message: no one would see the plot, and its server would stop with the script. Use mira_save() for a file, or give browser to open the plot anyway.

In MiRA, the plot can still be changed. MiRA's R button (Copy as R code, next to Save Session) shows the ggmira code for the current view, starting with the mira() call that made the plot, to paste into a script. What R cannot set is listed in comments under the code. By default the code ends with print(p, viewer = TRUE), which opens the plot in RStudio's Viewer pane; untick the box under the code for the browser.

Every printed plot is served by its own small server, on its own port. ggmira keeps the servers of the 10 most recent plots and stops older ones: an older plot stays on screen, but reloading its page fails. Print it again to reopen it.

Examples

library(emln)
net <- load_emln(17) # 4 layers; bird and plant nodes
#> Creating state node map
#> Creating extended link list with node IDs
p <- mira(net, bipartite = TRUE, setA_type = "bird")
#> Bipartite network: drawn as undirected. Use directed = TRUE for a directed one.

p        # the same as print(p)
#> Not opened: R is not interactive. Print the plot in an R session, or give `browser` to open it from a script.

print(p, port = 9000)            # another port
#> Not opened: R is not interactive. Print the plot in an R session, or give `browser` to open it from a script.
# print(p, browser = "chrome")   # another browser
# print(p, viewer = TRUE)        # RStudio's Viewer pane
# options(ggmira.viewer = TRUE)  # the pane for every plot
# print(p, mira_path = "~/MiRA") # a local copy of MiRA, not the bundled one

# When done, stop the servers the plots started
httpuv::stopAllServers()
